$schemaNote: One entry per distinct RBI data series/publication relevant to deposit-rate tracking. Each 'downloadEndpoints' entry was individually curl-tested in this research pass unless tested=False (found via search but not independently fetched here).

series.name: Structure of Interest Rates (Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy / Handbook of Monetary Statistics of India)
series.description: Annual, fiscal-year-end (as-at-end-March) snapshot of: call/notice money rate, 5-major-bank deposit rates (savings + 3 term-deposit buckets), 5-major-bank lending rates, MCLR, and (from FY2013-14) WALR/WADTDR for all SCBs excl. RRB/SFB.
series.startDate: 1970-71 (fiscal year); savings-deposit column starts FY2007-08 in the editions checked
series.releaseTiming: Each August-ish, as part of the annual Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy release (current edition dated 2026-07-31)

downloadEndpoints.label: 2007-08 to 2025-26 edition, Table 62 (HTML view)
downloadEndpoints.format: HTML table (RBI renders XLSX content server-side; also offers XLSX/PDF download links on the same page)

downloadEndpoints.label: 1970-71 to 2005-06, Handbook of Monetary Statistics of India, Table 39 (XLS + PDF)
Index of ALL annual editions
downloadEndpoints.format: HTML index page listing every edition's Table-59-equivalent XLSX/PDF

series.scriptableConclusion: YES - plain curl/requests with a browser-like User-Agent successfully fetched every URL tested above (HTML index pages, XLSX, legacy XLS, and PDF), no JS rendering needed.
series.notes: The table NUMBER changes almost every edition (39 -> ... -> 74 -> 64 -> 62 -> 59 across the editions sampled) as RBI inserts/removes tables elsewhere in the Handbook; always locate by TITLE ('Structure of Interest Rates'), not by number. Older editions must be fetched individually from the index page above since only ~20 years of history appear in any single edition's table.

series.name: Lending and Deposit Rates of Scheduled Commercial Banks (monthly press release + underlying Tables 1-9 workbook)
series.description: Monthly bank-group-wise (Public Sector / Private Sector / Foreign / All SCB) Weighted Average Domestic Term Deposit Rate (WADTDR) on fresh AND outstanding rupee term deposits (Tables 3-4), plus WALR fresh/outstanding (Tables 1-2), bank-wise and bank-group-wise 1-year MCLR (Tables 5-6), floating-rate benchmark mix (Table 7), and sector-wise WALR (Tables 8-9). Excludes RRBs and SFBs.
series.startDate: WADTDR/WALR bank-group time series in the workbook checked (July 2026 release) runs from March 2020 to the latest available month (June 2026 in that release, ~1-month publication lag); RBI's press-release TEXT summary (without the full workbook) goes back further in the RBI press-release archive but was not exhaustively checked in this pass.
series.releaseTiming: End of each month (this release, covering data 'received during July 2026' i.e. reflecting June 2026 figures, was itself dated July 31, 2026); also feeds the 'monthly' section of https://www.rbi.org.in/SCRIPTs/Statistics.aspx

downloadEndpoints.label: Index of ALL monthly releases (press-release PDFs; each release must be opened individually to find its own Tables-workbook link, filename pattern 'MLDRSCB' + date changes each month)

series.scriptableConclusion: YES for a given month once its press-release HTML page is fetched (the Tables-workbook URL is embedded as a plain <a href> in that page, filename pattern like 'MLDRSCB<DDMMYYYY>E.xlsx' -- a script must parse each month's press-release detail page to discover that month's exact filename, since the hash-free filename still encodes the release date). The RBI press-release-detail URL for a given prid (e.g. prid=63271 for July 2026) must first be located via ExaSearch or the SectionID=369 index; sequential prid numbers are NOT reliably one-per-topic (a nearby prid, 63259, turned out to be an unrelated same-day press release about the Second Amendment Directions -- confirmed by direct fetch in this pass -- so prid guessing is unsafe).
series.notes: This workbook does NOT contain a savings-deposit-rate range or bank-wise MEDIAN/MODAL term-deposit card-rate table as the task brief hypothesized -- only WADTDR (weighted-average, not median/modal) and MCLR. A median/modal card-rate series, if RBI publishes one, was not located in this pass; likely candidates for follow-up are the RBI Bulletin's 'Current Statistics' section and the discontinued/renamed Basic Statistical Return (BSR) publications -- both out of time budget this pass.

series.name: Database on Indian Economy (DBIE) - RBI's general statistical data warehouse
series.description: Web portal exposing (per RBI's own description) all RBI-published statistics including deposit/lending rates, organized under 'Financial Sector' etc., with Excel/CSV/PDF export per report.
series.startDate: Portal itself dates to 2001 per re3data.org metadata; underlying series have their own start dates
series.scriptableConclusion: NO (for this research pass) - a plain curl/requests GET on the portal root returns only the Angular app shell (empty <app-root>, JS bundle references, a `<base href="#">`), confirmed by direct inspection of the raw HTML in this pass. Actual report data loads via client-side JS calling internal APIs not identified in this pass. A script would need either (a) a headless browser, or (b) reverse-engineered JSON API endpoints (not investigated -- out of scope per the task's Browser-tool time limit).
series.notes: RBI's monthly press releases (see wadtdr_walr_monthly_press_release above) and the annual Handbook (see handbook_structure_of_interest_rates above) are far more practical machine-fetchable sources for the same underlying data than DBIE itself. Recommend building the tracker's pipeline against those two, and treating DBIE as a human-browsable cross-check only.
